target.title: Remove Kimi K2 and CrossModel provider relays
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the Kimi K2 and CrossModel hosted-relay integrations across app, CLI, widget, docs, locales, and tests
- tolerate retired provider IDs in persisted config by dropping unknown entries with a warning
- document hosted-relay eligibility and service caveats for Sub2API, Chutes, ZenMux, and T3 Chat
- fix Command Code billing navigation to use the generic settings route
- refresh provider counts and the social-card source/image

The CrossModel integration by @hujuncheng was solid. This removal is an operator-transparency policy decision, based on [identifiable operator, verifiable upstream authorization, and operating-track-record criteria](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/blob/54cfd1a3f504b74d8c438ace0131d81a9482d18c/docs/provider.md#hosted-relay-eligibility). Happy to restore the integration if CrossModel publishes an imprint and clarifies upstream authorization. Original integration: #1747.

## Verification

- `swift test --filter 'CommandCodeProviderTests|CodexBarConfigUnknownProviderTests'` — 4 tests, 2 suites passed
- `swift test --filter ProviderSettingsDescriptorTests` — 37 tests passed
- `make test` — 675 selections; 57/57 groups passed; no failures, retries, or timeouts
- source-blind config/roster contract — retired IDs dropped, known Codex state preserved, provider roster clean
- `./Scripts/regenerate-codex-parser-hash.sh --check` — current
- `node Scripts/check-site-locales.mjs` — 23 locales, 138 site messages
- `make check` — all gates passed; 0 SwiftFormat changes and 0 strict SwiftLint violations
- autoreview — clean; no accepted/actionable findings

No changelog edit; maintainer batch follows separately.

target.title: Add local session cost ledger
target.body: ## Summary Adds a local Codex session cost ledger that works alongside a managed Codex account. It exposes a clear Settings toggle for local session cost estimates, keeps the local scanner independent from the selected managed account, and avoids showing an account quota failure as a failure of valid local cost data. ## Problem Developers using organization-provided OpenAI API keys can run Codex but often do not have OpenAI organization billing or administrator access. The existing account-level quota paths cannot provide a useful spend view in that situation. The local session ledger is the appropriate source for this case. It reads the token records Codex already writes locally and produces an API-rate estimate without calling the OpenAI billing API. ## How it works CodexBar scans JSONL session files under `$CODEX_HOME/sessions` when `CODEX_HOME` is set, otherwise `~/.codex/sessions`. It takes the final `token_count` record from each session. For example: ```sh rg '"type":"token_count"' \ ~/.codex/sessions/2026/07/14/rollout-2026-07-14T16-38-08-.jsonl \ | tail -1 ``` The record provides total input, cached input, and output token counts. Cost calculation separates cached and uncached input: ```text uncached_input = input_tokens - cached_input_tokens cost = uncached_input * input_rate + cached_input_tokens * cached_input_rate + output_tokens * output_rate ``` Rates are per token in the calculation. The price catalog refreshes from models.dev when available and uses bundled pricing offline. The result is an API-rate estimate, not an organization invoice. Negotiated discounts, credits, taxes, and platform-side accounting can differ. ## Behavior - Shows 1-day and 30-day local token and estimated-cost totals. - Lists the contributing conversations with cost, model, input, cached input, output, and last activity. - Preserves per-model breakdowns for sessions that switch models. - Uses the existing on-disk scan cache for fast refreshes. - Keeps managed-account quota and web-dashboard behavior separate from the local ledger. - Suppresses the generic remote quota error when valid local Codex cost data is available. - Does not upload session content, require an Admin API key, or modify existing provider keys. ## Validation - `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer swift test --filter ProviderSettingsDescriptorTests` - `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer swift test --filter MenuCardModelCodexDegradedQuotaTests` - `CodexBarCLI cost --provider codex --refresh --no-color` against real local session logs - Installed the release build locally and verified the CodexBar menu and local cost view Closes #2174

## Problem

Kiro usage fetching fails for enterprise/IdC accounts because  passes  to the legacy  REST API, causing a  error.

## Root Cause

Enterprise credentials have a  that gets resolved via . When this ARN is passed to , the Kiro 0.9.2 version of the API rejects it as malformed. The same issue was fixed in [kiro.rs v0.6.11](https://github.com/ZyphrZero/kiro.rs).

## Solution

Added a new  that:
- Reads credentials directly from kiro-cli's SQLite database ()
- Makes direct HTTP calls to AWS Q  API
- Uses fixed  version in User-Agent (the version that doesn't require )
- **Does NOT pass ** - this is the key fix
- Falls back to CLI strategy if API fails

## Changes

- **New file**:  - Direct API fetch strategy
- **Modified**:  - Added API strategy as primary, CLI as fallback
